title: Constant approximation for submodular facility location
short_statement: For homogeneous submodular facility location, a 2026 preprint claims tight $\Theta(\log\log n)$ value-oracle approximability; arbitrary facility-specific functions are a different, harder model.
open_problem: Verify the 2026 claimed negative resolution for homogeneous value-oracle SFL. The previous arbitrary-$g_f$ formulation was already incompatible with a constant approximation under standard Set Cover hardness assumptions.
background: Facility location is a core operations research model for placing warehouses, servers, depots, and service centers. The classical fixed-charge model assumes a facility has one opening cost independent of which clients it serves. Many applications have richer economies of scale or shared-service effects: the marginal cost of serving an additional client may decrease, overlap with existing fixed costs, or depend on the mix of clients. Submodular facility location captures this by replacing a fixed opening charge with a monotone submodular function of the assigned client set. This is still a clean combinatorial optimization problem: the metric assignment term is classical, and submodularity is the standard mathematical abstraction for diminishing returns. The difficulty is that opening a facility and assigning clients are no longer separable. A local reassignment can change the submodular cost at many marginal scales, and the usual primal-dual and LP-rounding tools for fixed-charge facility location do not directly give constant factors. The exact model matters: the cited iterated-logarithmic guarantee assumes a common submodular function, with specified extensions; independent facility functions encode Set Cover. A 2026 preprint claims the homogeneous oracle threshold is also superconstant.
full_statement: Let $C$ be clients, $F$ facilities, and $d$ a metric on $C\cup F$. An assignment $\phi:C\to F$ has cost $\sum_c d(c,\phi(c))+\sum_f g_f(S_f)$, where $S_f=\phi^{-1}(f)$ and each $g_f$ is nonnegative, monotone submodular and zero at the empty set. Model correction: the earlier record allowed arbitrary different $g_f$ but attributed homogeneous results to that generalization. The constant-approximation question posed by the cited literature is for a SINGLE common value-oracle function $g_f=g$ at every facility. Arbitrary facility-specific functions already contain Set Cover and have logarithmic hardness. For common $g$, Abbasi et al. give $O(\log\log|C|)$; their extensions allow $p_f+g(S)$ on nonempty sets or $w_f g(S)$, not arbitrary unrelated functions. The historical question asks for a constant-factor polynomial-query approximation in the homogeneous model. Elmachtoub, Natura, and Neuwohner (October 2026), Theorem 2, claim an $\Omega(\log\log|C|)$ query lower bound even for common matroid-rank costs. This would answer that question negatively; it is a preprint claim, not independently proof-verified here.
known_results: Svitkina and Tardos developed hierarchical and submodular facility costs, logarithmic approximation, and constant-factor special cases. Abbasi et al. (ICALP 2024; preprint 2022), Theorems 1.1, 1.3 and 1.4, give $O(\log\log n)$ for a common function and its additive/multiplicative facility-weight extensions. They also improve universal stochastic facility location; classical metric facility location remains a related special case of the facility-weight variants. The unrestricted $g_f$ model already inherits Set Cover hardness. Elmachtoub, Natura, and Neuwohner (2026) claim matching oracle hardness for homogeneous SFL: polynomially many value queries cannot achieve $o(\log\log n)$ with constant success probability, even with unlimited computation. Version 2 (November 4, 2026), Appendix A, Corollary A.2, additionally reports computational hardness: unless $\mathrm{NP}=\mathrm{RP}$, no randomized polynomial-time algorithm with constant success probability attains $o(\log\log|F|)$ when the common matroid-rank function is supplied by a polynomial-size evaluation circuit. Note the facility-count parameter here, versus client count in Theorem 2. Neither statement automatically covers every specialized explicit representation.

progress.summary: Corrected homogeneous versus facility-specific models. A 2026 preprint claims a matching $\Omega(\log\log n)$ oracle lower bound for the homogeneous question.

counterexample_rationale: Hardness or integrality-gap examples could be finite metric/submodular instances, but proving oracle lower bounds may require a more elaborate construction.
alphaevolve_rationale: Search can explore small metric instances and submodular cost functions to test LP relaxations or rounding conjectures. It is less suited to proving a universal constant approximation.

literature.synthesis: The value-oracle lower bound and the circuit-representation hardness theorem require different access models. Version 2 covers both, under the qualifications in What Is Known. Arbitrary unrelated facility functions remain a separate, already harder generalization.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: Verify the new oracle lower-bound proof and its symmetry-gap construction. For further algorithmic work, specify a stronger representation or restricted cost family that avoids the oracle obstruction.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: Distinguish common $g$ from unrelated $g_f$ and value queries from explicit descriptions or stronger oracles. The new preprint's Theorem 2 allows unlimited computation but polynomially many value queries and requires constant success probability. Check monotonicity, submodularity, metric costs, and the lifted matroid-rank construction; this audit did not independently verify the proof. For v2 Appendix A, check the polynomial-size circuit representation and NP != RP assumption; do not replace |F| by |C| without a reduction.
